contract.note: Plain reading: about $500B in cumulative LLM costs since about 2017, plus material failures at checking against sources. Both are ordinary readings. The result turns on how costs are defined, which the speaker never stated.

evidence.note: April 2025 benchmark with sources supplied: the best model still had a 15% hallucination rate. This supports the capability part only.
2024 study of a specialised fact-checking model. It qualifies a reading of total incapability but sets no reliability threshold.
Annual private investment in generative AI for 2024. Wrong metric and period for cumulative LLM costs.
Annual data-centre capital spending in 2024. Wrong scope and period for cumulative LLM costs.

reviews.rationale: e1 supports the capability part: material failures with supplied sources as of April 2025. No evidence item gives cumulative LLM costs on a defined accounting basis, so the $500B part cannot be checked. Because the support condition needs both parts, the claim is unresolved.

semantics.note: A faithful historical comparison. 'Some predecessors' needs only one earlier model with a higher rate.

contract.note: Comparing measured hallucination rates on the same tasks is the ordinary reading.

evidence.note: OpenAI's release system card, a company disclosure, published April 2025: o3 hallucinated 0.33 vs 0.16 for o1 on PersonQA and 0.51 vs 0.44 on SimpleQA. o3's accuracy was also higher.

reviews.rationale: OpenAI's own release evaluation shows o3 with higher hallucination rates than o1 on both tests, which meets the support condition. Higher accuracy does not change the hallucination comparison. Persistence of the problem at the time of the post is consistent with this.

semantics.note: A faithful causal claim: mimicking human language leads to frequent mistaken belief that LLMs work like people.

contract.note: Plain reading: humanlike language causes people to wrongly attribute humanlike processes to LLMs. This is a fair reading, though what 'operate like people' covers is open to interpretation.

evidence.note: Speech modality raised anthropomorphism; first- vs third-person wording had no effect. Narrow manipulation that neither confirms nor refutes the broader claim.
In Turing tests, persona-prompted LLMs were often judged human. This shows successful imitation, not beliefs about how a known LLM works internally.

reviews.rationale: No evidence item measures whether humanlike language causes people to attribute humanlike cognition to LLMs. e1 and e2 measure related but different outcomes. The evidence neither establishes nor refutes the causal claim.
